a201.text: Day thirty-one. Our plant is drooping. Last time, Momo asked: is it sad?

a203.text: A drooping plant isn't sad. It needs something. Did you lock in your answer? Hold on to it.

a301.text: So the Buddies built a hotel on our window ledge. Three rooms. Three guests. Every guest must get everything it needs. By sunset.

a302.text: Three guests: our plant, our mealworm, and a mystery guest.

a303.text: It's You against the Buddies. You lock in first. Every time you are right, put up one finger on your other hand. No lock-in, no point. And a lizard is hiding in this video. Find it!

a401.text: Today you will learn what a drooping plant needs, why living things need water, and why living things need air.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

a501.text: Round one. Room one. The plant is drooping. What does it need? One, water. Two, food. Three, air. Show me with your fingers.

a503.text: Two, food! It's hungry. Give it my biscuit!

a504.text: One, water. I touched the soil. It is dry.

a505.text: One, water. Nobody watered it yesterday. But is it sad?

a601.text: Let's test Pip's idea. Pip waters the soil. Now we wait. This takes a few hours. So let's shrink down and follow the water. Quietly.

a602.text: You are tiny now. You are in the wet soil, with the water.

a605.text: All the way to a leaf.

a606.text: Plants need water to make food.

a701.text: A few hours later. Look! The plant is standing up again. The answer is one. Water.

a703.text: It is wilting. It does not have enough water.

a704.text: That is what the drooping was. The plant is not sad. It was wilting.

a706.text: Showed one finger? One finger up on your score hand!

a801.text: All living things such as plants and animals need water.

a802.text: The plant. The mealworm, with its juicy carrot. And you!

a803.text: We need water to digest food. We need water to carry out our daily activities. We need water to remove waste from our body.

a901.text: Room two is ready for our mealworm. A jar with a tight lid. Safe and snug!

a902.text: Something is not right with this room. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

a903.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! Look. The lid is shut tight. Air cannot get in.

a904.text: Our glass box has holes in its lid!

a905.text: Holes! I forgot. Sorry, little guest.

a906.text: A new lid, with holes, so air can get in.

a908.text: Living things breathe in air that contains oxygen.

a910.text: Now our guest can move in. Air, through the holes. Oats, for food. A juicy carrot, for water.

a911.text: All living things need air to live.

c1003.text: Water! Food! Air! Living things need all three!

a1101.text: Show me your score hand! Two fingers? You beat the Buddies. High five!

a1102.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the wall, above the hotel sign. Does a lizard need water? Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

a1202.text: The mealworm has oats. But nobody feeds a plant. So who feeds a plant?

a1203.text: Room three. A bean plant from Pip's dark cupboard. It had water every day. It had air. But something is wrong under this cloth. What is it missing? Find out in Part Two!
